title: the operator proofs run the host's bash, not the bare word bash
intention: Every operator proof builds its bash argv from the host's bash (shutil.which on Windows), and an AST door proof over cairn/devices/operator/proofs holds that no argv list starts with the bare word bash.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: git grep for a list literal headed by bash in cairn/devices/operator/proofs found 1 site(s): test_the_operator_verbs_are_in_its_bin.py:107
traces_to: Law 3 and Law 8: a proof that runs another OS's shell on a box measures that shell, not the component; Law 4: held by a scan.
how: In test_the_operator_verbs_are_in_its_bin.py add a module _BASH that is shutil.which('bash') on nt and 'bash' elsewhere and use it as the argv head at the 1 site(s). Add cairn/devices/operator/proofs/test_no_operator_proof_spawns_a_bare_bash.py, an AST scan of the operator proofs for a Call whose first argument is a list headed by the string bash. Other reds in these proofs are other causes and are left alone.

clauses.claim: an AST scan of cairn/devices/operator/proofs/test_*.py finds no Call whose first argument is a list headed by the string bash
the edited proofs name the host's bash (a _BASH head) at their spawn sites
